taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO as Ungnadia speciosa Endl.; the genus is monotypic under the current treatment.
look_here_first: Start with the leaves and fruit. Mexican buckeye has alternate odd-pinnately compound leaves, usually with several broad serrate leaflets, and a distinctive three-lobed woody capsule containing large glossy dark seeds. Pink spring flowers often appear before or with the new foliage.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Sapindaceae herbarium index includes three Ungnadia speciosa specimens. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Vascular Plants of Williamson County treatment. project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Only exact county documentation from herbarium/county-flora/WMA sources was counted.

best_field_traits: leaves alternate, odd-pinnately compound, without stipules
showy pink to rose-purple spring flowers, often before full leaf-out
fruit a conspicuous three-lobed/three-valved woody capsule
large glossy dark-brown to black seeds held inside the capsule
not a true Aesculus buckeye despite the common name
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate odd-pinnately compound leaves with opposite leaflet pairs plus a terminal leaflet; petiole base has a pulvinus.
morphology_keys.flower: Pink spring flowers are borne in clusters and are a useful seasonal cue, but fruit architecture is stronger for confirming the genus.
morphology_keys.fruit: A woody, usually three-lobed capsule that splits to expose large shiny dark seeds.
morphology_keys.field_tip: Do not confuse 'Mexican buckeye' with Aesculus. Ungnadia has alternate pinnately compound leaves and a three-lobed capsule; Aesculus typically has opposite palmately compound leaves.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against Aesculus: alternate pinnate leaves versus opposite palmate leaves. Against soapberry: Ungnadia makes a thick three-lobed capsule with large glossy seeds, while Sapindus makes translucent/fleshy one-seeded drupes. Against boxelder: Acer negundo has opposite compound leaves and paired samaras.
